anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Schema and Index Design Anomaly: Static mismatch between physical data model (table layout, partitioning, indexes, data types, constraints) and workload access patterns, forcing inefficient access paths.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: Optimizer chooses sub-optimal execution plans despite adequate statistics, due to cost-model or plan-reuse issues, causing erratic or poor performance.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: Physical corruption or logical inconsistency inside data or index pages breaks key ordering, page links, or heap-to-index mappings, making storage structures unreliable.

When all three anomalies arise together, the database exhibits extreme and confusing symptoms: queries oscillate between full scans and corrupt index probes, some result sets contain missing or duplicated rows, while others hang in long-running nested-loop storms or trigger sudden recompilations. Rebuilding or adding indexes may temporarily help a few statements yet make others worse, and integrity-check utilities intermittently report low-level page or key errors. Plan caches fill with divergent plans for the same statement, latch contention and I/O spikes appear without clear correlation to workload changes, and corrective actions aimed at any single layer fail to stabilize performance.

Causal chain: a poor schema/index design first pushes the optimizer toward heavy scanning or non-covering lookups; this increases I/O and page churn, heightening the likelihood of latent storage or index corruption surfacing under load. Corrupted pages then feed inconsistent cardinality and access-path signals to the optimizer, provoking highly variable or outright wrong plan choices and further amplifying performance variance. Conversely, unstable plan selection stresses already mis-designed structures with bursty access patterns, accelerating fragmentation and exposing more integrity flaws. The intertwined feedback loop among design flaws, bad plans, and physical corruption degrades both performance and correctness, making the composite anomaly far more severe than any individual root cause alone.

entry.official_definition: Aborts any statement that takes more than the specified amount of time; zero disables the timeout.
entry.trigger_condition: A SQL statement runs longer than statement_timeout, measured from command arrival until completion.
entry.workload_impact: The running statement is aborted; when configured, the timed-out statement is logged.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
